title: Table display with two Ultimaker 3D printers, laptop and tools
objects_and_counts: Two white Ultimaker 3D printers are visible on the table, positioned center-left and center-right. Both printers are shown as complete assemblies with visible filament guide tubes entering their tops.
One laptop computer is visible at the far left of the table; its screen is on and showing a 3D-modeling / printing application.
One green-and-black handheld power tool (branded 'Ultimaker' on its side) is visible at the far right of the table.
One single printed lattice sphere (grey) is visible on the table in front of and between the two printers (front-center).
At least two filament spools are visible stacked at the right rear of the table near the drill; a third spool or disk is partially visible below or behind them (see uncertainties).

A plate or small turntable with multiple small white printed parts is visible immediately to the left of the filament spools; the exact count of those small white printed parts cannot be determined from the image.
Two small metallic cylindrical items (appear to be nozzle or connector-like parts) are visible on the table in front of the filament spools and to the right of the lattice sphere.
Two hand tools (a pair of blue-handled pliers and an orange-handled cutting tool or screwdriver) are visible at the lower-right foreground on the table.
spatial_relations: The two Ultimaker printers are placed side-by-side near the center of the table, with a smaller printer at center-left and a taller printer at center-right.
The laptop sits to the left of the left/center printer, angled toward the viewer on the left edge of the table.
The printed lattice sphere is positioned on the table in front of and centered between the two printers.
The filament spools and a plate with small white printed parts are located to the right rear of the right/center printer, near the handheld power tool.

The green-and-black handheld power tool is at the far right of the table, to the right of the filament spools; two small metallic cylindrical parts are between the sphere and the spools, and two hand tools lie in the lower-right foreground near the power tool.
colours_and_materials: Both 3D printers are white with translucent or glass build-chamber panels and internal white illumination.
The table surface is glossy white and reflective.
The handheld power tool is green with black accents and has the 'Ultimaker' name in white on its side.
The printed lattice sphere is grey and appears to be a matte or slightly textured plastic or metal print (material not confirmed).
Filament on the spools appears translucent/white or clear.
The small metallic cylindrical parts appear silver-metallic.
uncertainties: No visible room name or number is present in the image; location is therefore unknown from image.

Some printed labels include additional characters that are partly obscured or too small to read; for example, model suffixes on the printers are partially legible as 'Ultimaker 3' and 'Ultimaker 3 Extended' but smaller text on machine panels is unreadable.
The exact number of filament spools is uncertain: at least two spools are clearly visible stacked, with a third spool or disk partially visible beneath or behind them.
The exact count of small white printed parts on the plate to the left of the spools cannot be determined from the image due to partial occlusion and distance.
The laptop screen contains additional UI text and labels, but only the word 'Ultimaker' is clearly legible; other on-screen text is unreadable from this view.
I have not attempted to infer equipment specifications, materials, or operational state beyond what is visually apparent.
